name: Digital waste receipt API connector for Scottish and Northern Irish sites
demand: The UK first phase covers approximately 12,000 permitted receiving sites, but the Scotland/Northern Ireland split of eligible sites is unverified (https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2026-10-12/debates/26101257000016/DigitalWasteTrackingMandatoryReportReceiptOfWasteService). Scotland has a rough proxy of 1,016 licensed sites for specified waste activities in 2023, excluding sites that do only landfill or incineration; this is not a phase-one customer count (https://www.gov.scot/publications/waste-reprocessing-infrastructure-scotland/pages/4/). A ministerial answer quoted by an MLA reports approximately 550 NIEA-authorised waste facilities, but that broader figure is not confirmed as a phase-one count (https://patsymcglone.com/2026/09/29/aqw-51979-22-27-number-of-high-risk-waste-sites/). Search volume, installs, unique users and paying users are unverified. IntelliWaste self-reports 1,000+ submissions and 3,000+ WTNs; the page gives no underlying event date or payer count, so treat this as an undated usage claim, not independent evidence (https://www.intelliwaste.co.uk/). Defra's published user research describes manual record creation as burdensome, but gives no willingness-to-pay measure (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/developing-the-digital-waste-tracking-service/digital-waste-tracking-service).
prices: Paid software is optional: operators can submit through the government spreadsheet route, and the government service charge is £26 per organisation per year (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/report-receipt-of-waste). Public competitor offers include AnyWaste Free Core with Defra submission and no subscription (https://anywaste.com/platform); LoadLog free for up to 5 WTNs monthly, then £12/month (https://loadlog.co.uk/pricing); WasteMatrix £30/month per site plus VAT (https://wastematrix.co.uk/); Tipslip £49/month for one site and £99/month for three (https://www.tipslip.co.uk/pricing); and Byrne at £89/month per site, with £70 for guided setup (https://byrnedigitalsolutions.co.uk/pricing). These are asking prices, not proof of sales. The practical software price floor is £0.
copy_speed: Copy speed is high. Dated first-party launch announcements include AnyWaste in May 2026 (https://anywaste.com/platform), First Mile's Miley on 9 September 2026 (https://www.thefirstmile.co.uk/the-big-picture/miley-the-waste-tracking-software), and A-Gas's RefHub on 1 October 2026 (https://www.agas.com/news-insights/refhub-launches-with-digital-waste-tracking-for-uk-customers/). These are launch claims, not evidence of customer uptake. The Defra provider list was updated 23 October 2026 and contains many listed products, though listing does not establish active sales or product quality (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/report-receipt-of-waste-choose-a-software-provider/report-receipt-of-waste-choose-a-software-provider).
platform_risk: High dependence on Defra's API and provider process: registration, test credentials, implementation of the API, PAT scenarios, self-certification and production credentials are required; the provider guide describes 14 test scenarios (https://defra.github.io/waste-tracking-service/production/api-register-as-a-software-provider/). The spreadsheet option is expected to remain available until at least October 2027, and the service also charges £26/year per organisation (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/developing-the-digital-waste-tracking-service/digital-waste-tracking-service; https://www.gov.uk/guidance/report-receipt-of-waste). Scotland's regulations are made and take effect 1 January 2027 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ssi/2026/145/contents/made). The Northern Ireland Assembly page still labels its proposed rule In Progress and shows no SR number or plenary outcome, despite the published January 2027 timetable (https://www.niassembly.gov.uk/assembly-business/committees/2022-2027/agriculture-environment-and-rural-affairs/legislation/delegated-legislation/2026/the-digital-waste-tracking-regulations-northern-ireland-2026/; https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/report-receipt-of-waste-choose-a-software-provider/report-receipt-of-waste-choose-a-software-provider).
defensible_asset: No exclusive data or rules asset is demonstrated. The API, reporting requirements and much regulator site information are public (https://defra.github.io/waste-tracking-service/production/api-register-as-a-software-provider/; https://www.sepa.org.uk/environment/waste/waste-data/waste-data-reporting/waste-site-information/). A defensible product could accumulate reliable permit-specific mappings, integrations with weighbridges or existing waste systems, and trusted audit history; these are potential assets, not established advantages. The free spreadsheet route and free or low-cost alternatives make a thin connector easy to replace (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/report-receipt-of-waste; https://anywaste.com/platform; https://loadlog.co.uk/pricing).
build_effort: Medium-high for a marketable connector; engineering hours are unverified. Work includes provider onboarding, API integration, the 14 PAT scenarios, production access, source-system data mapping, validation, error handling and an audit trail (https://defra.github.io/waste-tracking-service/production/api-register-as-a-software-provider/; https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/report-receipt-of-waste-choose-a-software-provider/report-receipt-of-waste-choose-a-software-provider). A generic receipt form is less work than supporting multiple weighbridge or ERP systems, but it competes directly with complete products already offering API submission (https://loadlog.co.uk/pricing; https://wastematrix.co.uk/).
channel: Prefer inbound search content, API documentation, a public demo and a listing on Defra's compatible-provider page after completing its process (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/report-receipt-of-waste-choose-a-software-provider/report-receipt-of-waste-choose-a-software-provider; https://defra.github.io/waste-tracking-service/production/api-register-as-a-software-provider/). Do not cold-message sole traders or certain partnerships: ICO guidance treats them as individual subscribers, and includes private social-media DMs as electronic mail; consent or the soft opt-in is required. Public online advertising and inbound content avoid that cold-message route (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guide-to-pecr/electronic-and-telephone-marketing/).
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified. No operating cohort or support-load evidence establishes that Ricardo can stay at or below 5 hours/week; integration setup and customer-specific support could exceed that limit.
desk_test: One-day, no-code test: publish a plainly labelled pre-launch page showing a sample receipt flow and a paid-pilot interest form; share it only in public waste-sector channels that allow vendor posts. Ask respondents for their site nation, permit status, current system and whether they would pay for the specific integration. Count only qualified, voluntary responses; do not cold-message individuals or sole traders. This tests interest, not proven recurring revenue.
red_flags: The mandate is verified, but the commercial gap is not: spreadsheet reporting is available, Defra's service fee is low, a free competitor offers submission, and a paid competitor starts at £12/month (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/report-receipt-of-waste; https://anywaste.com/platform; https://loadlog.co.uk/pricing). No dated, independently verified paid-revenue event was found; published prices and self-reported usage do not establish payment. The exact Scotland/NI addressable count and search demand are unverified. NI's legislative status adds date risk (https://www.niassembly.gov.uk/assembly-business/committees/2022-2027/agriculture-environment-and-rural-affairs/legislation/delegated-legislation/2026/the-digital-waste-tracking-regulations-northern-ireland-2026/). The automation field is 0 as a no-verified-measure sentinel, not a measured claim that actual automation is zero. Overall: the deeper evidence weakens the standalone connector case; validate a specific unsupported incumbent-system integration before building.
